g.text: Mathematics and assumptions

text.style: font-size: 10.3px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: Companion to strips 01–08 · supplied structure, derived consequences, explicit limits

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: What these pictures can establish
A proof sketch for a supplied classical model with one degree of freedom: local Hamiltonian structure and a
Noether example. This is not a derivation of mechanics from marks alone, nor of quantum mechanics or the supplied
alpha paper.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 01–04 · Comparing, composing, refining, returning
We supply an affine plane, comparison by translation, and reversible rotations. Tip-to-tail composition gives
vector addition. Strip 3 samples a prescribed differentiable path; drawings alone do not prove a smooth limit.
Strip 4 introduces cyclic position (angular phase), not the specialized geometric phase of transport/holonomy, and
not a quantum amplitude. It shows three intermediate directions and a return.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 05 · The extra structure that makes Hamilton possible
We now supply a STATE plane with dimensionless conjugate coordinates q,p and oriented area ω=dq ∧ dp. In strips
6–8 black measures q (right positive), green measures p (up positive); left/down are negative. The green tip
locates the state relative to the black tail. These are state components, not spatial directions. Conjugacy is
assumed, not established by a right angle. In physical units p dq has units of action. Momentum need not equal
velocity.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 05 → 06 · The local derivation
Let u,v be rates: a dot means change per unit time. Assume an autonomous (time-independent), C¹ (continuously
differentiable) rule preserving oriented area for EVERY small cell. Local expansion must cancel: ∂u/∂q + ∂v/∂p=0.
A partial derivative is a slope holding the other coordinate fixed. This lets one function H generate both rates.
Formally, α=u dp−v dq is closed: its integral around any sufficiently small closed loop vanishes. On a simply
connected patch (no holes), integrating α is path-independent and gives H. Thus
H is fixed up to a constant. Strip 5 illustrates the area hypothesis; it does not prove it for every rule.
Topology can obstruct a global H. Physical energy needs a physical model.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 06 · An exact turning rule
Choose H=(q²+p²)/2. The two rate panels use the SAME state (2.1,1.2), at the SAME instant. Orange lengths are 1.2
and 2.1 on a common rate scale. They are not successive kicks. The last panel joins each pair as in strip 2: three
exact states at times 0, 0.5, 1 share one origin and scale; pale means earlier. The exact evolution is
q′=q cos h+p sin h, p′=p cos h−q sin h.
This preserves ω and H. The Euler assignment (q+h p,p−h q) multiplies area and q²+p² by 1+h² instead. Circles
belong to this chosen example and scaling, not every Hamiltonian system.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 07 · A different rule and its continuous symmetry
Switch to H=p²/2: Φ_t(q,p)=(q+t p,p). The shift T_a(q,p)=(q+a,p) preserves the specified area (is canonical) and
H, so Φ_t T_a=T_a Φ_t. Both orders start at (2,0.65), use shift a=1.5 and time t=1, and end at (4.15,0.65). Pale
intermediate q values are 3.5 and 2.65. Grey always means shift; orange means slide. Strip 8 repeats the unshifted
run at times 0,1,2. The oscillator does NOT have this translation symmetry.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: 08 · The Noether charge and why it is conserved
Translation is generated by Y=∂/∂q; its pairing with ω gives dp, so the charge is J=p. Since H has no q
dependence, dJ/dt=ṗ=−∂H/∂q=0. Equivalently, use S=∫(p q̇−H)dt. Independent interior variations of q,p, with δq=0
at time endpoints, give Hamilton’s equations. Constant q translations preserve the action and map endpoint data to
translated data; they are not fixed-endpoint variations. Noether conservation holds along stationary trajectories.
Equal drawn marks alone do not prove this theorem.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #087f78

g.text: Limits and the remaining debt
Supplied: geometry, oriented pairing, regularity, the two model rules and variational hypotheses. Derived
conditionally: local Hamiltonian form, exact example flows and conserved translation charge. Not derived: the
earlier Genesis/L1 result, an identity of holonomy with Noether, quantization, Born weights, Everett branching or
Bell correlations. Novice comprehension remains to be tested.
